requirements.example: Section 7.1 of a pure-stress planar elasticity formulation paper: characterising ψ with manufactured solutions on A = [-3,3]×[-1,1]. There is no plate-with-hole, Cook membrane or L-shaped benchmark in this passage. It is linear isotropic elasticity with E = 200, in plane stress and plane strain. There are three manufactured displacement fields: shear u_s = (1/10) sinh(x) e2, bi-axial u_b = (1/10)[sin(x) e1 + sin(y) e2], and periodic u_p = (1/10)(sin[π(x+y)] e1 + sin[π(x+y)] e2). Plane stress uses ν ∈ {0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5}. Plane strain uses the same values except 0.5, which is replaced by ν = 0.499. Dirichlet conditions are applied on the whole boundary, and the matching body force is f = -Div σ̃. The quantity reported is the relative L2 stress error. Section 7.2 adds a spectrum study of the operator on [-1,1]^2 with Neumann conditions on the whole boundary. The convergence study for ν ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5} refers back to the 3D benchmark of Section 6.1, which this passage does not define, so it is not encoded here.

cases.name: Verification 1: isotropic thick cylindrical shell under radial Lorentz body force density, axial strain fixed (eps_z = 0)
unlisted_needs: Axisymmetric / generalized plane strain cylinder with eps_z = 0; ends axially fixed on a 1 m long shell; quarter azimuthal extent with symmetry planes
Radially varying body force density f(r) ≈ 5.69 GN/m^3·(r/1m) − 0.356 GN/m^3·(1m/r), from uniform axial current density jz = 95.1 MA/m^2 (Ampère + Lorentz)
Output is full radial profiles σr(r), σθ(r), σz(r) across r in [0.25, 0.5] m, and the resulting axial force Fz (< 0)
Cases with axial tension (eps_z > 0, Fz > 0) were run but not reported
reference_values: r1 = 0.25 m, r2 = 0.5 m, shell length 1 m
jz = 95.1 MA/m^2, B = 22.4 T, Pmag = 200 MPa
Model and Ansys stress profiles agree to within 0.7%

cases.name: Verification 2: two nested cylindrical shells (inner isotropic, outer transversely isotropic) under external pressure, eps_z = 0
unlisted_needs: Bonded two-layer (multi-material) radial interface at r2 = 0.67 m
Transversely isotropic outer layer (axis = z); transverse-transverse Poisson ratio 0.5
Generalized plane strain with eps_z = 0, producing a finite axial compression Fz
Output is radial stress profiles σr, σθ, σz(r); the passage is cut off before results or tolerances are given
reference_values: Inner layer: r1 = 0.33 m to r2 = 0.67 m, E = 200 GPa, nu = 0.3
Outer layer: r2 = 0.67 m to r3 = 1.0 m, Ez = 200 GPa, E_perp = 100 GPa, nu_z,perp = 0.3, nu_perp = 0.5

cases.name: Analytic case: uniform cylindrical shell with finite bore under external pressure (Lamé)
unlisted_needs: No geometry, material or load values are given; the check is the closed-form inner-edge hoop stress
reference_values: Any bore makes the allowable Pmag for steel half its value: 660 MPa → 330 MPa (B limit 40.7 T → 28.8 T)

cases.name: Analytic case: 3-layer coil (soft/stiff/soft) under external pressure
unlisted_needs: Three bonded layers with different Young's moduli; the passage gives no numerical values
The expected result is qualitative: σz and σθ are concentrated in the stiff middle layer, with σr = 0 at the inner edge and −Pext at the outer edge

quotes: The geometry is a uniform cylindrical shell with inner radius r1 = 0.25 m, outer radius r2 = 0.5 m.
The material has an isotropic Young's modulus E = 200 GPa and an isotropic Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
The axial strain is fixed to be z = 0, though due to Poisson effects this results in a finite axial compression Fz < 0.
One quarter of the azimuthal extent was simulated, with fourfold radial symmetry and axially fixed boundary conditions.
The model results agree with the Ansys results to within 0.7%
It has axial isotropic Young's modulus Ez = 200 GPa, transverse Young's modulus E⊥ = 100 GPa, axial-transverse Poisson's ratio νz,⊥ = 0.3, and transverse-transverse Poisson's ratio ν⊥ = 0.5.
The exterior is subjected to a pressure Pext = 200 MPa.
